name: Leg Weave Pass Completion
description: Leg Weave Pass Completion from Leg Weave keeps the knees folded while the passer frees the trapped leg, clears the hips and establishes a stable side pin.
summary: The leg-weave pass uses an arm threaded between the legs to bring the knees together, then clears the remaining foot or half-guard hook before settling into side control.
overview:
The top passer begins in Leg Weave, facing a knee shield or linked leg frame. The weaving limb is the arm. Securing that control is the entry checkpoint; a pass is complete only after the hips and remaining leg hooks are cleared.

Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee. Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint. Avoid leaving the weaving arm extended where the bottom player can sit up into a kimura.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Lachlan Giles — leg weave pass, no gi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9rDzchSk4fw); [Lachlan Giles — leg-weave counter demonstration](https://bjjfanatics.com/blogs/news/interesting-leg-weave-counter-with-lachlan-giles).

attacker.name: Leg Weave Pass Completion Attacker
attacker.description: Leg Weave Pass Completion (attacker): Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee. Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint.
attacker.overview:
The top passer begins in Leg Weave, facing a knee shield or linked leg frame. The weaving limb is the arm. Securing that control is the entry checkpoint; a pass is complete only after the hips and remaining leg hooks are cleared.

Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee. Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint. Avoid leaving the weaving arm extended where the bottom player can sit up into a kimura.

Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm. Remove the remaining foot or half-guard hook before establishing side control. If the bottom player turns or inserts a frame, keep control of distance and reset the pass rather than forcing a fixed angle.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Transfer hip control from the folded knees to the side-control hip block after the legs clear. Settle the crossface and upper-body connection without forcing the neck; completing the arm weave alone does not secure that pin.

Maintain an outside base: Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm.
Clear the legs before settling: Remove the remaining foot or half-guard hook before establishing side control.
Follow the hips: If the bottom player turns or inserts a frame, keep control of distance and reset the pass rather than forcing a fixed angle.

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (top): Which arm route supplies the weave at the start?
flashcards.answer: Thread the arm through the available leg gap and connect to the lower thigh or knee.
flashcards.answer_line: An arm passing between the opponent's legs

plausible: An arm scooping beneath both thighs together
An arm hugging the knees only from outside
trap: An arm pressing the upper shin while the lower knee is free

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (top): What should the shoulder and chest do to the leg frame?
flashcards.answer: Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint.
flashcards.answer_line: Bring the two knees together with supported pressure

plausible: Press only the upper shin while the knees stay apart
Spread the knees farther apart
trap: Shift chest pressure to the hips before securing the lower knee

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (top): Why keep the weaving arm from hanging far from your torso?
flashcards.answer: Avoid leaving the weaving arm extended where the bottom player can sit up into a kimura.
flashcards.answer_line: It can offer wrist-and-elbow access for a kimura

plausible: An exposed elbow deepens the knee pin without changing wrist access
The knee fold protects the arm even when the elbow leaves the ribs
trap: A straight arm is harder to encircle because the wrist stays far away

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (top): What should support your weight while your feet circle?
flashcards.answer: Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm.
flashcards.answer_line: A mobile base outside the folded leg frame

plausible: Your extended weaving elbow as the sole prop
Both feet together under the opponent's hips
trap: Your chest leaning past the arm with both knees left behind

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (top): What must clear before transferring to a side-control hip block?
flashcards.answer: Remove the remaining foot or half-guard hook before establishing side control.
flashcards.answer_line: The knee line and remaining foot or hook

plausible: The upper knee only, with your ankle still caught
Your hips past the shield while the lower foot stays attached
trap: The arm grip alone, leaving both legs beside your thigh

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (top): A new inside frame stops your angle. What is the next task?
flashcards.answer: If the bottom player turns or inserts a frame, keep control of distance and reset the pass rather than forcing a fixed angle.
flashcards.answer_line: Rebuild distance and a workable angle around the hips

plausible: Keep your feet planted and extend the weaving arm farther
Drop the knee grip and reach across the shoulder frame
trap: Lean farther through the same frame with a narrower base

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (top): Once the legs clear, how do the new pin controls divide the work?
flashcards.answer: Side control requires a new upper-body connection and hip block after the leg-weave phase.
flashcards.answer_line: Upper-body contact holds shoulders; hip block denies knees

plausible: Both hands keep the ankle grips while the shoulders remain free
The crossface controls the knees without a separate hip barrier
trap: The old weave restrains the shoulders after the legs have cleared

defender.name: Leg Weave Pass Completion Defender
defender.description: Leg Weave Pass Completion (defender): The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip. Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
defender.overview:
The top passer begins in Leg Weave, facing a knee shield or linked leg frame. The weaving limb is the arm. Securing that control is the entry checkpoint; a pass is complete only after the hips and remaining leg hooks are cleared.

The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip. Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together. Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.

Prevent the passer from flattening your shoulders while controlling the legs. An underhook can help you face the passer and rebuild half guard when the shoulder line is not already pinned. Do not wrench a knee out of a fixed weave; create room with the hips and frames first.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

A late guard recovery still needs an inside shoulder frame before a small hip escape returns the knee. If you rise with an underhook while the weave loosens, follow the opponent's overhook pressure with a stable facing base instead of allowing your arm to separate from the hip.
key_principles: Recognize the arm weave: The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip.
Keep the shield supported: Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
Recover inside space: Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.
Deny upper-body collapse: Prevent the passer from flattening your shoulders while controlling the legs.
Use an available underhook: An underhook can help you face the passer and rebuild half guard when the shoulder line is not already pinned.
Move the whole leg: Do not wrench a knee out of a fixed weave; create room with the hips and frames first.

Use aligned shoulder pressure and chest pressure to bring the knees together without twisting the knee joint.
Move the hips and feet without collapsing all weight over the woven arm.

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (bottom): Which early contact should you identify as the weave?
flashcards.answer: The passer's arm connecting your legs is the relevant control, not a leg threaded across your hip.
flashcards.answer_line: An opposing arm joining your upper and lower leg frame

plausible: An opposing hand on only the top shin
Two opposing arms scooping below both thighs
trap: An opposing arm clasping both knees from their outer surface

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (bottom): What prevents the shield becoming an unsupported knee?
flashcards.answer: Maintain a useful knee angle and upper-body frame before the passer folds the legs together.
flashcards.answer_line: An upper-body frame backing the knee angle

plausible: Both elbows stretched away toward the mat
Letting the shoulders flatten while leaving the knee up
trap: A knee pulled close while both hands chase the ankle

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (bottom): With the weave loosening, how do you restore the knee barrier?
flashcards.answer: Move the hips and pummel the knee back between the bodies while the weave is still loose.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame, shift the hips and pummel the knee inside

plausible: Pull the passer's neck while leaving hips immobile
Reach for their far ankle while both shoulders flatten
trap: Lift the upper knee alone while the hip remains under pressure

flashcards.question: Leg Weave Pass Completion (bottom): Why keep your shoulder free during late recovery?
flashcards.answer: Avoid combining folded legs with a flat shoulder pin; keep a frame to recover facing space.
flashcards.answer_line: You need room to face the passer behind your frame

plausible: Flattening the chest lets the near knee circle around the weave
The foot angle alone creates space even while the shoulders are pinned
trap: Keeping the shoulder pinned gives the framing arm more room to work
